title: Odd-level Fourier weight of majority
statement: For $m,k\in\mathbb N$ with $k$ odd, let $M_m$ be the majority function on $\{0,1\}^{2m+1}$ that is $1$ when more than $m$ coordinates are false and $-1$ otherwise. Its Fourier weight at level $k$ is $\displaystyle W_k[M_m]=\binom{2m+1}{k}\left(\frac{\binom{m}{(k-1)/2}}{\binom{2m}{k-1}}\cdot\frac{\binom{2m}{m}}{2^{2m}}\right)^2$, with the quotient interpreted as real division, including when its denominator is zero.
replaced:
Let $m\in\mathbb N$, put $n=2m+1$, and define $M_m:\{\pm1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ by
$M_m(x)=1$ when more than $m$ coordinates equal $1$, and $M_m(x)=-1$ otherwise.
For $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$ define
$\widehat M_m(S)=2^{-n}\sum_{x\in\{\pm1\}^n}M_m(x)\prod_{i\in S}x_i$, and for every
$k\in\mathbb N$ define $W_k(M_m)=\sum_{|S|=k}\widehat M_m(S)^2$.
For every odd $k\in\mathbb N$, put $r=(k-1)/2$; then
\[
 W_k(M_m)=\binom{2m+1}{k}
 \left(\frac{\binom mr}{\binom{2m}{k-1}}
            \frac{\binom{2m}{m}}{2^{2m}}\right)^2,
\]
where $\binom ab=0$ for $b>a$ and a real quotient with zero denominator is interpreted as zero.
